title: Materialize bounded relation catalogs by declared cardinality
finding: GPU-45 required CompiledRelationBlocks.blocks to be a bounded Sequence before normalization, but tuple(sequence) still delegates to an arbitrary __iter__ implementation and therefore can consume more items than the sequence's declared len. The explicit signatures path had the same iterator-materialization shape and also did not reject non-Sequence iterables with a stable fail-closed ValueError before len/normalization. That left the catalog boundedness contract dependent on iterator behavior instead of declared cardinality.

implementation.summary: Add one private in-owner _materialize_declared_sequence helper that indexes exactly range(len(sequence)). Reuse it for both compiled receipt blocks and explicitly requested relation signatures. The signatures boundary now requires an actual bounded Sequence before cardinality validation. Existing error strings, MAX_COMPILED_RELATIONS limits, canonical sorting, duplicate checks, semantic validation, compiler outputs, receipt family, and public API remain unchanged; no second compiler, receipt family, validator subsystem, cache, index, backend, registry, semantic plane, or remote branch was added.
implementation.gardener_note: one private normalization helper replaces two direct tuple-iterator materializations inside the existing owner

focused_contracts: a declared-empty CompiledRelationBlocks Sequence is normalized without invoking its iterator
a non-empty explicit RelationSignature Sequence is materialized by declared index cardinality without invoking its iterator
an unbounded explicit signature iterable is rejected as not a bounded Sequence before it can be consumed
existing cardinality limits, sorting, duplicate rejection and semantic validation remain authoritative after bounded materialization
